issues.legal_issue: In the absence of a contrary agreement, co-mortgagors contribute to the mortgage debt in proportion to the value of their respective shares or parts of the mortgaged property, not equally or according to the benefit each received.
material_facts: Several co-owners mortgaged property in which they held distinct ownership interests.
One co-mortgagor's separately owned property was used to satisfy the common mortgage debt.
The co-mortgagors disputed how their respective shares of the debt should be calculated, and no contrary agreement was established.
issues.conclusion: Contribution is to be calculated rateably according to the value of each co-mortgagor's interest in the mortgaged property.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 82 and 92 of the Transfer of Property Act specifically govern contribution and subrogation between co-mortgagors and, as the special law, exclude section 43 of the Contract Act, which concerns joint promisors generally. Section 82 prescribes the conditions for contribution, so equitable allocation according to benefits received cannot replace its statutory method. The Court relied on Ganesh Lal v. Charan Singh for the rule that extrinsic principles cannot modify the statutory contribution scheme; it also referred to Rani Chhatra Kumari v. Mohan Bikram and Mohammad Sher Khan v. Seth Swami Dayal on the statutory character of mortgage rights, and to Hira Singh v. Jai Singh and Taibai v. Wasudeorao on excluding equitable considerations in statutory mortgage matters.

predicates.co_mortgage_contribution_case: The proceeding concerns contribution between persons who jointly mortgaged property.
predicates.co_owners_have_distinct_property_interes: The co-mortgagors own distinct shares or parts of the mortgaged property.
predicates.no_contrary_contribution_agreement: The co-mortgagors have no established agreement that sets a different basis for sharing the debt.

issues.definition: When co-owners jointly mortgage property and have no established agreement for another allocation, their contributions are determined by the values of their respective property interests.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged oral agreement altering the statutory basis of contribution is not established by the interested testimony of one participant where the other participant who could corroborate it is not called and the contemplated written terms remain unsigned.
material_facts: The defendants relied on an alleged oral agreement between the co-mortgagors to allocate liability according to the benefit each received from the borrowing.
The only witness supporting the alleged agreement was a defendant who was an interested participant in it.
The other person said to have been present was not called as a witness.
A draft of the proposed terms was unsigned and uninitialled, and the evidence indicated that the parties had contemplated reducing the arrangement to writing.
The trial judge accepted the testimony based on its apparent probability, while the appellate courts assessed the circumstances and found the agreement unproved.
issues.conclusion: The alleged agreement was not proved and could not displace the statutory basis for contribution.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the credibility and inherent probability of the evidence, including the failure to call an available participant and the unsigned draft. It relied on Virappa v. Periakaruppan for the qualification that deference to a trial judge's assessment of a witness does not prevent appellate courts from reassessing a finding based on inherent probability when they are equally able to evaluate that matter.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_contribution_agreement and alleged_agreement_supported_only_by_interested_witness and corroborating_participant_not_called and contemplated_terms_left_unsigned

predicates.appeal_concerning_contribution_agreement: An appeal concerns whether an agreement between co-mortgagors changed their respective contribution obligations.
predicates.alleged_agreement_supported_only_by_inte: The only testimony supporting the alleged agreement comes from an interested participant in it.
predicates.corroborating_participant_not_called: Another person said to have been present and able to support the account is not called to testify.
predicates.contemplated_terms_left_unsigned: The parties contemplated written terms, but the draft was left unsigned and uninitialled.

issues.definition: In an appeal about a contribution agreement, an account supported only by an interested witness is not established where an available corroborating participant is not called and contemplated written terms remain unsigned.

issues.legal_issue: A co-mortgagor who satisfies the common mortgage debt may obtain property-based relief through subrogation without an inter-mortgagor personal covenant, where the pleadings in substance seek a mortgage decree and the relief causes no prejudice.
material_facts: The plaintiff's separately owned property and its rents were used to satisfy the mortgage debt and related costs.
The plaintiff sought personal relief against the other co-mortgagors and also sought a declaration of charge and a decree for sale under the mortgage procedure.
There was no personal covenant between the co-mortgagors.
Although the pleading did not expressly use the term subrogation, the charge and mortgage-decree claims in substance sought relief against the other mortgaged property.
The plaintiff's claim specified a maximum amount sought from each defendant.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff could not obtain a personal decree against the other co-mortgagors, but the claim could proceed as a subrogation-based mortgage claim; the amount and property liabilities were to be determined on remand, subject to the amounts claimed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 92 and 82 of the Transfer of Property Act, a redeeming co-mortgagor may obtain the mortgagee's relevant rights against the mortgaged property, with contribution determined rateably under section 82. Order XXXIV rule 2 of the Civil Procedure Code provides for a mortgage decree. The Court treated the substance of the pleadings as sufficient to seek that relief despite the omission of the word subrogation, where no prejudice was caused, but held that the absence of a personal covenant precluded personal relief. The Court directed inquiry into the payment attributable to the mortgage, contractual interest, and the values of the mortgaged properties, and limited any defendant's liability to the amount claimed against that defendant.

rule.if: co_mortgagor_redemption_proceeding and redeeming_owner_paid_common_mortgage_debt and no_personal_covenant_between_mortgagors and pleadings_substantially_seek_mortgage_property_relief and no_prejudice_from_pleading_form

predicates.co_mortgagor_redemption_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a co-mortgagor who has satisfied a common mortgage debt and seeks recovery from the other co-mortgagors.
predicates.redeeming_owner_paid_common_mortgage_deb: The redeeming co-mortgagor's property or its income was used to satisfy the common mortgage debt.
predicates.no_personal_covenant_between_mortgagors: The co-mortgagors made no personal promise to pay one another's shares of the debt.
predicates.pleadings_substantially_seek_mortgage_pr: The pleading, in substance, seeks a charge or mortgage decree against the other mortgaged property.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_pleading_form: Granting the property-based relief despite the way it was pleaded causes no prejudice to the opposing parties.

issues.definition: A co-mortgagor who pays the common debt without a personal covenant may obtain property-based relief when the pleading substantially seeks it without prejudice, but recovery cannot exceed the amount claimed.
